title: Check if a text message you've received from HMRC is genuine
text:
If your text is not listed here check HMRC contact that uses more than one communication method .

 Report suspicious phone calls, emails or texts to HMRC .

 Branded messages

 HMRC may send branded text messages to some of our customers. These will look different to our standard text messages.

 These branded messages will:

 • show HM Revenue and Customs as the sender

 • include the HMRC logo

 • contain the verified sender’s information

 You should also read our guidance on how to identify suspicious contact .

 If your device is not compatible to receive a Rich Communication Services (RCS) message the branded message will appear as a standard text message.

 Links in text messages

 HMRC does send text messages to some of our customers.

 In the text message we might include a link to GOV.UK information or to HMRC webchat.

 HMRC will never ask for personal or financial information when we send text messages.

 We advise you not to open any links or reply to a text message claiming to be from HMRC that offers you a tax refund in exchange for personal or financial details.

 To help fight phishing scams, you should send any suspicious text messages to 60599 (network charges apply) or email:  phishing@hmrc.gov.uk  then delete them.

 Child Benefit

 HMRC may contact you by text message to confirm:

 • we have received your Child Benefit claim

 • we have received your request to extend your Child Benefit claim

 • you have successfully opted into or out of Child Benefit payments

 • a change to your account

 • a claim has been successful

 Confirmation and update text messages

 HMRC may contact you by text message to confirm that we have received from you:

 • a claim

 • a form

 • other correspondence

 Corporation Tax — follow up to your Corporation Tax helpline call

 HMRC may send you a text message if you have called the Corporation Tax helpline and we have your mobile phone number stored. The message will:

 • give a summary of what was discussed during the call

 • confirm your query is being processed

 • give an expected timescale

 We’ll contact you if we need any more information, you do not need to contact us again.

 Debt Recovery

 From 15 June 2026 up to and including 14 December 2026 HMRC may contact you by text message.

 HMRC may send you a text message to tell you:

 • that we have not got your payment and we’d like to help you avoid any further penalties or interest

 • to call us about a credit on your account

 • that we’ve asked your bank or building society to hold some money in your business account

 Fast parcel operator drivers — interview reminder

 HMRC may send you a text message to:

 • confirm that a letter was sent to you about an interview

 • remind you to book a telephone appointment

 The text message will not:

 • ask for personal or financial information

 • link directly to any websites

 International debt customers

 From 21 September 2026 up to and including 19 March 2027, HMRC may contact you by text message.

 HMRC may send you a text message if we have not received your payment.

 The message will ask you to:

 • 
 check your online account to see what you owe

 • 
 make any overdue payments to avoid interest

 • 
 search for ‘non-resident payment enquiries’ on GOV.UK

 PAYE Settlement Agreement

 From 28 February 2026 HMRC may contact you by text message.

 HMRC may send you a text message if you have called the PAYE Settlement Agreement Employer helpline to:

 • summarise what you discussed in the call

 • confirm that your query is being processed 

 • give you an expected timescale

 We’ll contact you if we need any further information, you do not need to contact us again.

 PAYE or Self Assessment complaints

 From 27 April 2026 HMRC may contact you by text message.

 HMRC may send you a text message if you have made a complaint about PAYE or Self Assessment to:

 • tell you that your complaint is being reviewed

 • tell you that someone will call you the next day to discuss your complaint

 • explain that when we call you our number may show as withheld

 You do not need to contact us.

 Retirement annuity relief

 From 29 September 2026 HMRC may contact you by text message.

 HMRC may send you a text message if we have written to you about a retirement annuity relief claim.

 The text message will ask you to:

 • review your retirement annuity relief claim

 • check the contributions shown on your 2024 to 2025 tax return

 • correct your tax return if any information is wrong

 The text message will not:

 • ask for personal or financial information

 • include links to websites

 Self Assessment penalty appeals

 HMRC may send you a text message if you appeal against a Self Assessment penalty.

 The text message will confirm:

 • that your appeal has been reviewed

 • when you can expect the outcome

 These text messages will not:

 • ask for personal or financial information

 • provide any links to websites

 Self Assessment tax refunds

 HMRC may send you a text message if you request a Self Assessment tax refund.

 The text message will confirm:

 • that your tax refund is being processed

 • when you can expect to get it

 The text message will not:

 • ask you for personal or financial information

 • provide any links to websites

 Survey after a call to HMRC or a compliance check

 HMRC may send you an exit survey by text message if you have:

 • agreed to provide feedback after calling one of our contact centres

 • gone through a compliance check

 This text message will not:

 • ask for personal or financial information

 • include any phone numbers

 • provide links to websites other than to the survey platform

 Tax refund — P800

 HMRC may send you a text message saying you’re due a tax refund (also known as a P800 refund) if they’ve sent a letter and have not had a response.

 It will not:

 • ask you for personal or financial information

 • provide any links to websites

 Find out how to claim your refund .

 Other texts you should check

 You can also check text messages listed in HMRC contact that uses more than one communication method .
changeNote: Information about ‘Retirement annuity relief’ has been added.
